note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 67; A06b Const 67; L05 Const 70(1)(a)-(d), PNG 6C): ordinary naturalisation after 8 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Constitution of the Independent State of Papua New Guinea (Parliament of Papua New Guinea, linked from https://parliament.gov.pg/constitution-of-png/), Part IV Citizenship, ss. 64-70. Every figure the file holds now rests on it, and the dataset is no longer cited. This copy's s. 64 bars dual citizenship outright; the dataset's exception for citizens of designated countries (Citizenship Act s. 6C, 2014) isn't in it, and the form doesn't hold it.

sources.title: Constitution of the Independent State of Papua New Guinea (Parliament of Papua New Guinea, linked from https://parliament.gov.pg/constitution-of-png/), Part IV Citizenship, ss. 64-70
sources.said: 66. CITIZENSHIP BY DESCENT. (1) A person who– (a) is born in the country on or after Independence Day; and (b) had one parent who was a citizen ... is a citizen. (2) A person– (a) who is born outside the country on or after Independence Day; and (b) who had one parent who was a citizen ...; and (c) whose birth is registered as prescribed by or under an Act of the Parliament ... is a citizen. 67. CITIZENSHIP BY NATURALIZATION. (1) A person who has resided continuously in the country for at least eight years may apply ... (2) To be eligible for naturalization, a person must– ... (g) renounce, in such manner as is prescribed by or under an Act of the Parliament, any other citizenship and make the Declaration of Loyalty. ... 70. AUTOMATIC LOSS OF CITIZENSHIP. (1) A citizen who has reached voting age and is of full capacity who– (a) obtains the nationality or citizenship of another country by a voluntary act (other than marriage); ... loses his citizenship.
